transcript.text: To clarify the relationship between my load testing findings and Morgan's reservation requirement: the 6 warm workers I measured is the minimum needed to keep processing latency within target during the expected burst pattern, given the 11-minute cold start. That's a floor, not a ceiling — it doesn't conflict with Morgan's 18 baseline workers for the reservation commitment. In fact, 18 baseline workers would exceed the 6-warm-worker minimum, which is fine from an SRE latency perspective. The more urgent issue is the scale-out threshold: the draft says trigger at 100 queued jobs, but my testing shows we need to trigger at exactly 40 queued jobs. With an 11-minute startup time, waiting until 100 jobs are queued would blow past our latency target before new workers even come online. So my recommendations are: baseline of at least 6 warm workers (Morgan's 18 satisfies this), and scale-out triggered at exactly 40 queued jobs instead of 100. I'll file this in the capacity review formally once we settle on the reconciled numbers.
